questions.text: Does the manufacturer publish the full composition of the product?
questions.hint: Look for a complete material/fibre list, including blends, coatings and finishes. A partial list is 'no'.

questions.text: Is the raw material for this fabric from recycling (e.g. recycled polyester fibre) or from certified crops (e.g. organic cotton)?
questions.hint: Look for recycled-content percentages or certificates such as GOTS, GRS, RWS, FSC/PEFC (lyocell). Vague claims like 'eco' or 'natural' are not enough.

questions.text: Was the product manufactured in the same region of the world where it is sold (local/regional production)?
questions.hint: Compare the country of manufacture with the market of the sale page. Answer 'na' only if local production is not possible for this product type.
questions.applicability: if possible for this product type

questions.text: Does the manufacturer publish carbon footprint data (Carbon Footprint)?
questions.hint: Look for a stated CO2e value, an EPD or an LCA summary for the product. A general sustainability pledge is not a footprint.

questions.text: Does the manufacturer provide an ISO 14001 environmental management certificate?
questions.hint: Look for an ISO 14001 mention or certificate for the manufacturer or production site.

questions.text: Does the manufacturer's website give information about water or energy savings in the production process?
questions.hint: Look for concrete statements or figures about reduced water or energy use in production.

questions.text: Does the manufacturer state that it holds, or works with fabric suppliers that hold, a European ecolabel or an OEKO-TEX certificate?
questions.hint: Look for OEKO-TEX Standard 100 / Made in Green or EU Ecolabel. Ideally with a certificate number that can be verified.

questions.text: Does the material NOT require chemical impregnation (e.g. for flame retardancy)?
questions.hint: Answer 'yes' if the product is not chemically treated. Answer 'no' if flame-retardant, stain-resistant or antibacterial finishes are used. Answer 'na' if no such treatment is needed for this product type.
questions.applicability: if needed for this product type

questions.text: Is the fabric free from harmful PFC/PFAS compounds ('forever chemicals'), e.g. in stain-resistant coatings?
questions.hint: Look for an explicit PFAS/PFC-free statement or a certificate that excludes them. Stain-resistant finish without such a statement is 'unknown'.

questions.text: Is the fabric a mono-material (100% one fibre), enabling full mechanical recycling?
questions.hint: Check the composition: 100% of a single fibre type. Blends such as polyester-cotton are 'no'.

questions.text: Does the manufacturer provide information about the recyclability of the product?
questions.hint: Look for recycling instructions, take-back schemes or recyclability statements for this product.

questions.text: Is the fabric 100% suitable for reprocessing after the end of its use?
questions.hint: Look for a statement that the whole product can be recycled or reprocessed, including trims and coatings.

questions.text: Does the manufacturer offer samples before purchase, which reduces the risk of mistakes and returns?
questions.hint: Look for a free or paid sample/swatch service.

questions.text: Is there information that the material is easy to clean with home methods, without specialist chemical cleaning?
questions.hint: Look for care instructions such as machine washable, spot-clean with water.

questions.text: Does the manufacturer state the fabric's abrasion resistance (min. 25,000 Martindale cycles)?
questions.hint: Answer 'yes' only if a Martindale value of 25,000 or more is stated. A lower value is 'no'. No value is 'unknown'.
